summary: Round 2's fixes land as described. Paths are folded one way for the decided list, the files clause covers an ask the reshape newly raises, the override test reads the round's own overrides, and the block says a decided fix keeps a task of its own. The findings sit on the edges of those same lists. A second resolve set off by a reshape's call for an override replaces that finding's list. The ask rules still match paths in the unfolded form. Two docs sentences no longer match the code: the resume section, and the record of what was shown before #106. No scheduled or queued work touches the files this diff changes (the repository has no routes/console.php).

findings.title: The 'Before #106' sentence names only a deferral the person typed as shown its first-planned task
findings.description: R1-2's fix (b3da1ea, round 1) changed the history sentence in 'A reshape after your decision' to: 'Before #106 a deferral you set yourself (`<id>: defer. <reason>`) was shown its task as first planned, and every other finding you or the autopilot decided was shown the shaper's list from before the decision, then the reshape's own.' That fixed the overstatement R1-2 reported, but the new wording is now too narrow. The base condition was `return decision && shown.disposition === 'defer' ? { ...shown, files: plannedFiles(f.id) } : shown` (origin/main, effectiveDispositions), where `shown.disposition` is the decision's own disposition when it names one and otherwise the disposition of the current `shaped`, which after a reshape is the reshape's. `plannedFiles` then read `taskFilesOf(resolvedTasks, id)`, the resolve's task. So the first-planned task was also shown for (a) an answered call that a reshape re-sorted to `defer`, and (b) a call whose decision names `defer` (no skill path writes one, as the loop test's `forcedDefer` comment says). The sentence tells the reader that both were shown the shaper's list. This is the record of old behaviour only; the current behaviour the bullet describes is right. The cause is in round 1's fix, not in round 2's.
findings.proposedFix: Reword the sentence to say that before #106 a decided finding was shown its task as first planned whenever it was shown as a deferral (a deferral you set yourself, a call whose decision names defer, or a call a reshape re-sorted to defer), and the shaper's list from before the decision otherwise, then the reshape's own.

findings.title: Resume section still says every shape-stage resume rewrites the four spec files
findings.description: The resume paragraph says 'A resume at the shape stage reruns the shaper, which rewrites the four spec files and never touches `redline/`.' This pull request adds a shape-stage stop for which that is false: the hold after a reshape (errors opening 'the reshape left ', workflows/redline-loop.js:4151-4158). `resumeLine` gives that resume the correct-in-place clause instead of the from-scratch one. Rule 9 of agents/redline-shaper.md (line 8 of the fix diff) and the 'A reshape after your decision' bullet (docs/running.md:127) both say so: 'read plan.md and shape.md as that attempt left them ... correct the task the error names'. So docs/running.md now gives two different accounts of the same resume. A person who reads only the resume section could expect the folder to be rewritten from scratch and act on that, for example by setting the decided entries aside before relaunching. #117 tracks changing the code for the other shape-stage stops, which would change the rest of this sentence later. It does not track this sentence being wrong today for the hold. Line 208 is not in this pull request's diff; the change elsewhere made it inaccurate.
findings.proposedFix: Qualify the sentence in the resume paragraph of `docs/running.md`, for example 'which rewrites the four spec files and never touches `redline/`, except after the hold of a decided finding's task, where it corrects that task in place ("A reshape after your decision" above)'.

findings.title: A reshape's paths are folded for the decided list but matched raw against the paths ask rules
findings.description: R2-2's fix made `cleanPaths` (492) trim each path, fold repeated slashes and `./` segments, and then call `relPath`. It left `relPath` (483) itself unchanged, and `ruleForPaths` (534-544) still reads each path through `relPath` alone: no trim, no slash folding, no `./` segment folding. The same reshape list is now read two ways. `forceAskRules` (3336-3338) matches the shaper's raw `files`, while the reshape loop stores `cleanPaths(listed.files)` in `decidedFiles` (4128, 4136), which the plan approver and the implementer are shown. Traced: with a paths rule `app/billing/**`, `globToRegExp` gives `^app/billing/.*$` (502-531). A reshape that lists a decided fix's task as `app//billing/charge.php` (or `app/./billing/charge.php`, or ` app/billing/charge.php`) does not match, so `record.forced` is not set and the finding stays tracked rather than being left to the person. `decidedFiles` then holds `app/billing/charge.php`, a path under the rule, and the hold passes it as a task with files. The remaining layers are the plan approver's rule 5 and the guard. The forcing miss on a non-canonical path existed before this pull request, since `relPath` never folded. What changed in round 2's fixes is that the stored and shown form now differs from the form the rules matched, and the decided block now asks for exactly these task paths. Round 2's shape.md Decision 1 left `relPath` alone on purpose ('a question no finding of this round raises'). Conditions: a paths rule, and an agent that writes a path under it in a non-canonical form.
findings.proposedFix: Match the paths rules on the cleaned form: in `ruleForPaths`, read each path through the same folding (`cleanPaths([path])[0] || ''`, lower-cased), or have `forceAskRules` pass `cleanPaths(files)`. Add a loop case: paths rule `app/billing/**` and a reshape that lists a decided fix's task as `app//billing/charge.php`, expecting the finding to be left to the person under the rule.

findings.title: A reshape's call for an override's finding re-resolves it and replaces its list with the second resolve's tasks alone
findings.description: `raised` (4161) is every judgment call the reshape returned whose id is not in `calls`. Overrides are never in `calls` (`overridesFor`, 3807), so a reshape that returns an override's finding as an ask with a call puts that id in `raised`. `openRaised` (4179) leaves it out of the stop only because it is in `decisions`. `resolveWith(raised, [], ...)` (4188) then counts it in `applied` (3846), and line 3999-4001 sets `decidedFiles[id] = taskFiles(id)`, where `taskFiles` reads only this resolve's `out.tasks` (3974). The list the first resolve and the reshape set is replaced. The removed `resolvedTasks` read every resolve's tasks together (origin/main: `resolvedTasks.push(...out.tasks)` and `plannedFiles = ... taskFilesOf(resolvedTasks, id)`). Traced for a defer override whose first resolve planned `app/x.php`, with a reshape that lists `app/x.php` for it but returns it as a call. If the second resolve does not restate that task, `decidedFiles['R1-1']` becomes []. No hold runs for a deferral. Plan approver pass 2 and the implementer are shown `["defer",[]]`, where the base showed `["defer",["app/x.php"]]` while plan.md still holds the mitigation. That disagreement between the list and the plan is the one #106 describes, which the approver's rule 1 bounces. If a commit of its own lands, the end-of-run warning reads 'the resolve agent planned no task with files for it' (4362), which is false. If the second resolve plans elsewhere, the list moves with no 'the reshape changed' warning and no `reshapedTasks` entry, so the cap's `reshaped` detail and `emptyBy` misreport it. A defer override reaches all of this. A fix override with no restated task stops at stage `resolve` (`namedUnplanned`, 3991-3994). The path is reachable: the R2-5 case `overrideCalled` (tests/loop-test.mjs:3463) runs `resolve r1 #1` for such a finding, but the mock resolve plans `app/x.php` for every id in its prompt, so no case shows the replacement. The comment at 3821-3825 ('a reshape that raises a call runs a resolve for that call alone ... so an earlier decision keeps the list its own resolve gave it') does not hold for an override. Conditions: a reshape that returns a call for a person's override (against the prompt's 'a decision the person made ... stays as it is'), and a second resolve that returns no task, or another task, for it.
findings.proposedFix: In resolveWith, set the list only for an id that has none yet: `for (const id of applied) { if (!(id in decidedFiles)) decidedFiles[id] = taskFiles(id) }`, so the first resolve and each reshape stay the only writers for an override's finding. Or keep an override's id out of `raised` (`!isOverride(call.id)`) so no second resolve applies it. Pin it with a defer override that a reshape returns as a call (`reshapeAsk: ['R1-1']`), and a mock key that scripts the second resolve's tasks by label (`resolveFilesAt: { 'resolve r1 #1': { 'R1-1': [] } }`). Expect plan approver pass 2 to be shown `["defer",["app/x.php"]]` and no 'planned no task' warning.

list.summary: After a reshape returns a judgment call for a finding the person overrode, the plan approver's next pass and the implementer can be shown no files for a decided deferral's mitigation. plan.md still holds that mitigation and the reshape kept it, so the run also warns falsely that the resolve agent planned no task. The cause is `for (const id of applied) decidedFiles[id] = taskFiles(id)`: the second resolve (`resolveWith(raised, ...)`, line 4188) counts the override's id as one it applied, because `raised` takes any call not in `calls` and overrides are never in `calls`. Its tasks then replace the list the first resolve and the reshape set, where the removed `resolvedTasks` combined every resolve's tasks; a second resolve that does not restate the existing task empties the list, and one that plans elsewhere moves it with no warning and no entry in `reshapedTasks` (so the cap's `reshaped` detail and `emptyBy` misreport it). Fix: in the second resolve, leave the list alone for an id it applies that already has one (an override), or merge with the existing list instead of replacing it; pin it with a defer override that a reshape returns as a call, whose second resolve returns no task for it.
list.failure_scenario: Plan dial; R1-1 is overridden to defer, and the first resolve plans its mitigation in app/x.php. The plan approver bounces. Following an adjustment, the reshape lists R1-1's files as app/x.php but returns it as an ask with a judgment call. `raised` contains R1-1, `openRaised` filters it out because `decisions` already holds it, and `resolve r1 #1` runs and returns no task for R1-1. Confirmed in a scratch copy of the harness: before this branch, plan approver pass 2 and the implementer were shown ["defer",["app/x.php"]] with no warning; on this branch both are shown ["defer",[]] and the result warns 'R1-1 has a commit of its own (1bbbbbb) and the resolve agent planned no task with files for it'.

list.summary: The resume section still tells the person that every shape-stage resume 'reruns the shaper, which rewrites the four spec files'. That is no longer true for the stop this PR adds: a resume after the hold ('the reshape left ...') is told to keep plan.md and shape.md and correct the task in place, as line 127, `resumeLine` and rule 9 of the shaper file now say. Fix: qualify the sentence ("except after the hold of a decided finding's task, where it corrects the task in place"), or point to the 'A reshape after your decision' bullet; #117 will change the rest of this sentence later.
list.failure_scenario: A decided fix's task is emptied by a reshape, so the run stops at stage shape and can be resumed at `reshape r1 #1`. A person reading the resume section expects the shaper to rewrite the folder from scratch, and may commit or set aside the decided entries before relaunching, while the run itself tells the shaper to keep them. The two documented behaviours contradict each other.

list.summary: The new bullet's history sentence says that before #106 only 'a deferral you set yourself (`<id>: defer. <reason>`)' was shown its task as first planned. The removed condition (`decision && shown.disposition === 'defer'`) also covered an answered call that a reshape re-sorted to defer, and a call whose decision names defer. Fix: say that before #106 a decided finding was shown its first planned task whenever it was shown as a deferral (by an override, by a call's own disposition, or by a reshape's re-sort), and the shaper's list otherwise.
list.failure_scenario: An answered judgment call that a reshape returned as `defer` was shown the resolve agent's task files under the old code. The docs say only a disposition the person typed was, so the record of the old behaviour that R1-2 corrected is still incomplete.

list.summary: The same reshape list of a decided finding's files is now read two ways. The workflow stores the folded form in `cleanPaths` (doubled slashes and `./` segments folded), and `forceAskRules` matches the raw form through `relPath`, which folds neither. Since #106 the decided block asks for the task's paths, so a task under a paths rule can escape the forcing at the reshape while the stored and shown path is under the rule. Fix: give `ruleForPaths` the same folding (one of the cleanup's own form cases per rule), or run `forceAskRules` on the cleaned list. Round 2's Decision 1 left `relPath` alone on purpose, as a question no finding of that round raised; this is that question.
list.failure_scenario: Paths rule `app/billing/**`. A reshape lists a decided fix's task as `app//billing/charge.php`. `relPath` keeps the doubled slash, the glob does not match, and the finding is not left to the person. `decidedFiles` stores `app/billing/charge.php`, which the plan approver and the implementer are shown. The guard then refuses the write and the round stops at implement, instead of the finding being left to the person at the reshape.
